This is the first script one should run before using any R scripts or genotyping functions. All editable settings are in the YAML header above or in Master_Pipeline.Rmd (settings_01), with comments explaining the settings. All paths are written from the project folder (Full_workflow), except full paths for preinstalled tools. 
After completing this script, move on to 02_ObiTools4_Basic_Visualisation.Rmd



## Settings, paths and basic setup
Chunk contains settings, paths to the installed tools and a timing function for speed optimization analysis.

```{r setup}
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
})

# Uploading shared functions
source("Code/R_scripts/asp_functions.R", local = TRUE) 

# Empty timing log for calculating elapsed time, all the scripts use the same shared function
timing_log <- list() 

# Settings come from the params block in the YAML header, this turns them into usable variables
invisible(list2env(params, envir = environment()))

# Paths to the installed Dorado and ObiTools4 directories so R can find the commands
login_shell_path <- tryCatch(system2(Sys.getenv("SHELL", "/bin/zsh"), c("-ilc", shQuote("echo $PATH")), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE, timeout = 10), error = function(e) "", warning = function(w) "") # PATH from the user's terminal settings, RStudio does not read them
tool_search_folders <- unique(path.expand(c(obitools_bin_folder,  # YAML folders first, a set path always wins
                                            if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("CONDA_PREFIX"))) file.path(Sys.getenv("CONDA_PREFIX"), "bin"), # active conda environment first
                                            strsplit(tail(c("", login_shell_path), 1), ":")[[1]],
                                            rev(Sys.glob(path.expand(c("~/*/bin", "~/*/*/bin", "~/*/*/*/bin")))), # unpacked anywhere in the home folder, newest version first
                                            Sys.glob(path.expand(c("~/*conda*/bin", "~/*conda*/envs/*/bin", "~/mambaforge/envs/*/bin"))), "/usr/local/bin", "/opt/homebrew/bin", Sys.glob("/opt/*/bin"))))

needed_tools <- c("obimultiplex")
tool_folders <- sapply(needed_tools, function(tool) {
  found_in <- tool_search_folders[file.exists(file.path(tool_search_folders, tool))]
  if (length(found_in) == 0) stop(tool, " not found. Install it, or paste its bin folder into the YAML (dorado_bin_folder / obitools_bin_folder)")
  found_in[1]
})

Sys.setenv(PATH = paste(c(unique(tool_folders), Sys.getenv("PATH")), collapse = ":")) # only the folders that hold the tools are added
cat("Using:\n", paste(file.path(tool_folders, needed_tools), collapse = "\n "), "\n")

tool_paths <- Sys.which("obimultiplex")
if (any(tool_paths == "")) stop("not found: ", paste(names(tool_paths)[tool_paths == ""], collapse = ", "),
                                ". Install it, or paste its bin folder into dorado_bin_folder / obitools_bin_folder in the YAML")
cat("Using:\n", paste(tool_paths, collapse = "\n "), "\n")

barcode_numbers <- sprintf("%02d", seq_len(n_barcodes))
demultiplexed_folder <- file.path("Data/Processed_data", dataset_name, "Demultiplexed_sequence_data")
dorado_output_folder <- file.path(demultiplexed_folder, "Dorado_demultiplexed_by_sample")
dir.create(dorado_output_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
identified_folder <- file.path(demultiplexed_folder, "Identified_sample_sequences_Obi4")
unidentified_folder <- file.path(demultiplexed_folder, "Unidentified_sample_sequences_Obi4")
dir.create(identified_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(unidentified_folder, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Settings used each run saved directly inside the output folder, useful for reproducibility
settings_used <- data.frame(setting = c("run_date", names(params)),
                            value = c(format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                                      vapply(params, function(setting_value) paste(setting_value, collapse = ", "), character(1))))

write.table(settings_used, file.path(demultiplexed_folder, "Dorado_demultiplexed_by_sample/settings_used_01.tsv"), sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
write.table(settings_used, file.path(demultiplexed_folder, "Identified_sample_sequences_Obi4/settings_used_01.tsv"), sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
write.table(settings_used, file.path(demultiplexed_folder, "Unidentified_sample_sequences_Obi4/settings_used_01.tsv"), sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
```


## NGSFilter file importing and cleaning 
This chunk imports the NGSfilter file needed for ObiTools4 obimultiplexing. The file is made by hand beforehand (primers, sample tags and all @param settings such as matching, primer_mismatches or primer specific mismatches) and its path is set in ngsfilter_path. The chunk cleans the file (trailing commas and spaces, spaces around commas, Windows line endings, empty lines), because these can cause problems in obimultiplex. It saves the cleaned version over the original.

::: {.alert .alert-warning}
!Important note!: the sample column can be filled with a basic "sample" tag. It could have been filled with sample names, but that would mean every single sample would need a different ngsfilter so it is properly named in the first lines of the .fastq header. This is not actually necessary, because the header also contains the barcode names, plus every file is already named after its barcode (barcode01-06-24). Future scripts extract the barcode name from the file name, so the generation of multiple per sample NGSFilter files is not needed.
:::

```{r NGSfilter_File_Importing_and_Cleaning, class.output = "scroll-output"}
if (!file.exists(ngsfilter_path)) stop(sprintf("ngsfilter file not found: %s", ngsfilter_path))
ngsfilter_start <- Sys.time()

ngsfilter_raw_lines <- readLines(ngsfilter_path, warn = FALSE)

# cleans every line and strips the trailing commas and spaces which can cause problems in obimultiplex
ngsfilter_clean_lines <- sub("^\ufeff", "", ngsfilter_raw_lines) # invisible BOM character Excel puts at the start
ngsfilter_clean_lines <- gsub("\r", "", ngsfilter_clean_lines) # Windows line endings
ngsfilter_clean_lines <- gsub("[ \t]*,[ \t]*", ",", ngsfilter_clean_lines) # spaces around commas
ngsfilter_clean_lines <- sub("[, \t]+$", "", ngsfilter_clean_lines) # trailing commas and spaces
ngsfilter_clean_lines <- sub("^[ \t]+", "", ngsfilter_clean_lines) # leading spaces
ngsfilter_clean_lines <- ngsfilter_clean_lines[ngsfilter_clean_lines != ""] # empty lines
ngsfilter_clean_lines <- sub("^(@param,[^,]+,)(TRUE|FALSE)$", "\\1\\L\\2", ngsfilter_clean_lines, perl = TRUE) # Excel saves true/false as TRUE/FALSE, obimultiplex needs lowercase

# one shared NGSfilter file for every barcode, the cleaned version is saved over the original
writeLines(ngsfilter_clean_lines, ngsfilter_path)
cat(sprintf("NGSfilter cleaned and saved: %s (%d lines)\n", ngsfilter_path, length(ngsfilter_clean_lines)))
cat(head(ngsfilter_clean_lines, sum(grepl("^@param", ngsfilter_clean_lines)) + 2), sep = "\n") # Prints all the param settings and first locus
log_time("ngsfilter.csv import and cleaning", ngsfilter_start)
```



## Second demultiplexing: ObiTools4 Demultiplexing
This chunk does the ObiTools4 obimultiplexing, it executes the bash command line function in R similar to the previous chunk. It uses the cleaned NGSFilter file with STA and LSP primers. It loops through all the samples and separates identified and unidentified reads into separate folders.

```{r Second_Demultiplexing_ObiTools4_Demultiplexing, class.output = "scroll-output"}
# loops through all the samples and separates identified and unidentified reads
for (barcode_number in barcode_numbers) {
  barcode_fastq_path <- file.path(dorado_output_folder, sprintf("barcode%s.fastq", barcode_number))
  if (!file.exists(barcode_fastq_path)) {
    cat(sprintf("barcode%s: input not found, skipped (%s)\n", barcode_number, barcode_fastq_path))
    next
  }

  obimultiplex_command <- sprintf("obimultiplex --tag-list %s --fastq %s -o %s -u %s",
    shQuote(ngsfilter_path),
    shQuote(barcode_fastq_path),
    shQuote(file.path(identified_folder, sprintf("barcode%s_identified.fastq", barcode_number))),
    shQuote(file.path(unidentified_folder, sprintf("barcode%s_unidentified.fastq", barcode_number))))

  obimultiplex_start <- Sys.time()
  obimultiplex_exit_status <- system(obimultiplex_command)
  if (obimultiplex_exit_status != 0) cat(sprintf("barcode%s: obimultiplex FAILED, see the output above\n", barcode_number))
  log_time(sprintf("barcode%s: obimultiplex", barcode_number), obimultiplex_start)
}
# The NGSFilter this run used, copy is saved next to identified sequences so the wrong primer hits analysis chunk can't accidentally use identified sequence and a different modified NGSFilter file which would give wrong results.
invisible(file.copy(ngsfilter_path, file.path("Data/Processed_data", dataset_name, "Demultiplexed_sequence_data/Identified_sample_sequences_Obi4", "Applied_NGSFilter_file.csv"), overwrite = TRUE))
```



## Timing Summary

```{r Timing_Summary}
# timing breakdown for speed optimization analysis
stage01_timing <- do.call(rbind, timing_log)
write_tsv(stage01_timing, file.path(demultiplexed_folder, "Identified_sample_sequences_Obi4/timing_log_01.tsv"))
write_tsv(stage01_timing, file.path(demultiplexed_folder, "Unidentified_sample_sequences_Obi4/timing_log_01.tsv"))
stage01_timing$step_type <- sub(".*: ", "", stage01_timing$step)
stage01_timing_summary <- aggregate(seconds ~ step_type, data = stage01_timing, sum)
stage01_timing_summary$seconds <- round(stage01_timing_summary$seconds, 2)
stage01_timing_summary
```
